summary_paragraph: A man with a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and polysubstance abuse was admitted for gross hematuria while on anticoagulation and after a recent fall. He experienced a syncopal episode during admission, resulting in loose teeth that required extraction. Workup revealed no acute intracranial or spinal injury, no pulmonary embolism, and no source of hematuria on renal ultrasound. His hematuria resolved without intervention, and anticoagulation was continued. He developed hypoxemia and radiographic findings consistent with pneumonia, for which he was treated with levofloxacin. Heart failure was managed with diuresis, and his warfarin was bridged with heparin and enoxaparin. He was discharged on adjusted anticoagulation, antibiotics for dental care, and optimized heart failure therapy, with plans for outpatient follow-up including lung function testing and palliative care evaluation.
